tasks.description: Shape an idea, then turn it into working code.

tasks.label: Design interfaces
tasks.description: Visual direction, layout, components and interface quality.

tasks.label: Motion
tasks.description: Web and mobile animation, from first idea to review.

tasks.description: Secure implementation, review and threat modeling.

tasks.description: Markdown, documentation, handoffs and research notes.

tasks.label: Working with agents
tasks.description: How agents split work, delegate and control cost.

startingPoints.task: Build a feature from a rough brief
Get a second opinion on my code
Design a screen that doesn’t look generic
Check a change in a real browser

skills.name: yeknal-implement
skills.title: Implement
skills.purpose: Takes a scoped feature or fix from plan to working code while keeping the rest of the repository behaving as it did.
skills.description: Implement a scoped feature or fix end to end while preserving repository behavior. Use when the user asks to build, change, add, or repair code; not for the closing gates, review, or publication, which is `yeknal-finalize`.
whenToUse: You want a feature built or a bug fixed from start to finish.
The change has to fit existing conventions and not break other behaviour.
You want the work verified rather than just written.

example.ask: Add CSV export to the reports page.
example.outcome: It reads how the page works today, adds the export following existing patterns and runs the flow to confirm it works.

skills.name: yeknal-review
skills.title: Code review
skills.purpose: Reads code or a whole system for real defects, regressions and maintainability risks, then sorts what it finds by severity and effort.
skills.description: Review code or systems for concrete defects, regressions, and maintainability risks when the user requests an audit or quality assessment.
whenToUse: You want a second opinion before merging.
A system needs a quality assessment.
You want findings you can act on, not style nitpicks.

example.ask: Review the payments module for bugs and risky code.
example.outcome: It reports concrete defects with locations and reasons, ranked by severity, and suggests fixes.

skills.name: yeknal-frontend-design
skills.title: Frontend design
skills.purpose: Sets a distinctive visual direction for new or heavily reshaped UI, from typography and composition to palette and interface copy.
skills.description: Create distinctive visual direction for new or substantially reshaped UI. Use for typography, composition, palette, interface copy, and anti-generic frontend design.
whenToUse: You are designing a new screen or product surface.
A design looks generic and needs a clear point of view.
Typography, colour and layout need to work as one system.

example.ask: Design the pricing page so it doesn’t look like every other SaaS template.
example.outcome: It sets a visual direction from the product’s content, picks type and colour roles and builds the page with real copy.

attribution.credit: Adapted from Anthropic’s frontend-design skill. Its library guidance credits Rare UI, which requires attribution if you install one of its components.

skills.name: yeknal-troubleshoot
skills.title: Troubleshoot
skills.purpose: Works back from a reproducible error, failing build or slowdown to its cause before it suggests a fix.
skills.description: Diagnose code, build, performance, deployment, or system failures from reproducible evidence when the user reports an error or regression.
whenToUse: Something broke and you don’t know why.
A build or deployment fails with an unclear error.
Performance got worse after a change.

example.ask: The app crashes when I open the settings page. Figure out why.
example.outcome: It reproduces the crash, traces it to the cause, fixes it and confirms the page opens.

skills.name: yeknal-playwright
skills.title: Browser automation
skills.purpose: Lets your agent open a real browser from the terminal to click through a flow, fill forms, take screenshots and read what’s on the page, so it can show you a change working.
skills.description: Automate a real browser from the terminal for navigation, forms, snapshots, screenshots, extraction, or UI-flow debugging.
whenToUse: You want proof that a sign-up, checkout or settings flow still works after a change.
A layout problem only shows up at one screen size or after a few clicks.
You need screenshots or page text captured the same way every time.
skills.avoid: If you want a permanent test suite in the repository, ask for Playwright test files instead, because this skill drives the browser from the command line.
skills.requirements: Needs Node.js with npx, which the bundled wrapper uses to run playwright-cli.

example.ask: Open the sign-up page at phone width, fill the form with test values and send me a screenshot of the confirmation screen.
example.outcome: It opens a browser through the bundled wrapper, steps through the form, saves the screenshot and reports anything that overlapped or clipped.

attribution.credit: Adapted from Microsoft’s playwright-cli skill, including its NOTICE.txt attribution.

skills.name: yeknal-testing-strategy
skills.title: Testing strategy
skills.purpose: Keeps verification end to end: proves behavior through the real entry point, bans new unit tests, and asks before any isolated check.
skills.description: Use before writing or running tests to enforce end-to-end-only verification. Do not write unit tests; prove behavior through the real entry point, keep a repeatable artifact, and report what stayed unverified.
whenToUse: You are about to add tests for a feature.
You want coverage of real user flows and error paths.
An agent is about to write unit tests instead of an end-to-end flow.

example.ask: Plan how we should test the new password-reset flow.
example.outcome: It maps the flow's real end-to-end path and failure states, then proposes the browser or CLI run that proves them and leaves a rerunnable record.

skills.name: yeknal-redesign-existing-projects
skills.title: Redesign an existing product
skills.purpose: Refreshes the look or flow of a working site or app without breaking its behaviour or the data behind it.
skills.description: Redesign an existing website or app without breaking behavior or data flow. Use for visual refreshes, UX improvements, responsive repair, or de-genericization.
whenToUse: A product works but looks dated or generic.
Responsive layouts are broken and need repairing.
You want UX improvements without rewriting the app.

example.ask: Give the admin dashboard a visual refresh without changing how anything works.
example.outcome: It inventories every route and state first, then restyles them while keeping each feature behaving the same.

attribution.credit: Adapted from Leonxlnx’s taste-skill collection. Its library guidance credits Rare UI, which requires attribution if you install one of its components.

skills.name: yeknal-animate
skills.title: Web animation
skills.purpose: Adds purposeful, accessible motion to components, pages, scrolling, gestures, SVG and canvas, with sensible timing and a reduced-motion fallback.
skills.description: Implement purposeful, accessible web motion. Use for new component, page, scroll, gesture, SVG, or canvas animation; use review-animations to audit existing motion.
whenToUse: You are adding an entrance, transition or gesture to a web interface.
A component needs motion that explains a change instead of decorating it.
You want motion that stays smooth and respects reduced-motion settings.
skills.avoid: To audit motion that already exists, use Review animations instead.

example.ask: Animate the settings drawer so it slides in from the right and can be interrupted halfway.
example.outcome: It picks the properties, duration and easing, builds an interruptible transition and adds a reduced-motion version.

attribution.credit: Written for this catalog, drawing on Emil Kowalski’s design-engineering ideas as inspiration; no source was copied.

skills.name: yeknal-application-security
skills.title: Application security
skills.purpose: Designs or hardens security across web apps, APIs, cloud setup, CI/CD pipelines and AI features, covering the OWASP-style risks a product is likely to face.
skills.description: Design or harden application security across web, API, cloud, CI/CD, and AI systems. Use for secure implementation or broad AppSec analysis.
whenToUse: You are building authentication, authorization or an API that handles user data.
A project needs a broad security pass before launch.
You want secure defaults for headers, secrets, rate limits and logging.

example.ask: Harden the API before we launch: auth, rate limiting, headers and how secrets are handled.
example.outcome: It reviews each area against concrete risks, fixes what it can and lists anything that needs a decision from you.

skills.name: yeknal-git
skills.title: Git
skills.purpose: Handles status, diffs, branches, commits, merges and pushes while leaving unrelated work in your checkout alone.
skills.description: Run the specific Git operation the user asked for while preserving unrelated work: status, diff, branch, commit, merge, history, or push. Not the full delivery flow, which is `yeknal-finalize`.
whenToUse: You want a focused commit without sweeping in other changes.
You need help with a branch, merge or history question.
Your working tree has unrelated edits that must survive.

example.ask: Commit only the API changes and push them to a new branch.
example.outcome: It stages just those files, writes a clear commit message, creates the branch and pushes it.

skills.name: yeknal-project-handoff
skills.title: Project handoff
skills.purpose: Keeps a short HANDOFF.md at the root of the repository so the next session, or the next person, can pick up exactly where the work stopped.
skills.description: Create, update, or resume work from a concise repository-root HANDOFF.md so another agent can continue without the current conversation. Use for substantial ongoing projects, milestones, and task handoffs.
whenToUse: A project spans several sessions or people.
You are finishing a milestone and want the context saved.
You are picking up an unfamiliar repository.

example.ask: Update the handoff with where we got to today.
example.outcome: It records the current state, decisions, how to verify the work and what remains, without repeating what the code already shows.

skills.name: yeknal-gh-address-comments
skills.title: Address PR comments
skills.purpose: Works through the review and issue comments on the open GitHub pull request for your current branch, using the GitHub CLI.
skills.description: Address review and issue comments on the open GitHub PR for the current branch using the `gh` CLI. Verifies `gh` auth first and asks the user to authenticate if needed.
whenToUse: A pull request has review comments waiting.
You want each comment addressed or answered in turn.
You use the gh CLI and want the agent to read the PR directly.
skills.requirements: Needs the GitHub CLI signed in to your account.

example.ask: Address the review comments on my PR.
example.outcome: It checks gh is signed in, reads each comment, makes the changes and summarises what it did for each one.

skills.name: yeknal-agent-cost-control
skills.title: Agent cost control
skills.purpose: Measures what agent work actually costs, finds the sessions and settings that own the spend, and changes one lever at a time without quietly losing review quality along the way.
skills.description: Cut agent inference spend without losing quality. Use when an LLM bill or per-task cost is too high, sessions feel expensive, or you are choosing models, effort, or caching.
whenToUse: The inference bill rose, or one task cost far more than expected.
You are choosing models or effort levels and want evidence rather than a hunch.
Someone asks whether prompt caching, model routing, or a cheaper tier will actually help.
skills.avoid: It does not decide who does the work and it does not review code. It will not present a saving without an outcome check that nothing important was dropped.

example.ask: Why did last month cost more than the month before, with the same workload?
example.outcome: It reads the harness usage log, shows that one long session carried most of the spend, checks whether caching is already warm, and recommends splitting the work at a boundary instead of switching models.

skills.name: yeknal-agent-readable-site
skills.title: Agent-readable site
skills.purpose: Gives every public page a markdown version and gives agents the files that explain the site: llms.txt, llms-full.txt, ai.txt, head signals and a crawler policy, plus a checker that separates host-blocked requirements from real failures.
skills.description: Use when a public site must be readable and quotable by AI agents: per-page markdown, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, ai.txt, head signals, crawler policy and a coverage check. Not content strategy or keywords.
whenToUse: You want AI agents and answer engines to fetch your pages cheaply and attribute them correctly.
You are adding llms.txt, llms-full.txt or ai.txt and want them generated rather than hand-maintained.
You need to know which parts of an agent-readable surface your host can actually support.
skills.avoid: It does not choose keywords, rewrite pages or promise citations. Query and metadata work stays with content SEO, and a published file is never reported as a visibility result.

example.ask: Make our whole site readable by AI agents and show me which pages still have no markdown version.
example.outcome: Every public route gets a markdown endpoint from the existing data loaders, the site files generate from one config, and the checker reports per-route coverage with the host's real limits named.

skills.name: yeknal-animate-expo
skills.title: Animation in Expo
skills.purpose: Builds animation for React Native and Expo apps with Reanimated, Gesture Handler, Expo Router and haptics, making the decisions that decide whether motion feels right on a device.
skills.description: Build animations in React Native and Expo with Reanimated, Gesture Handler, Expo Router and expo-haptics, covering gestures, sheets, press feedback, haptics, and screen transitions. For web motion use `yeknal-animate`.
whenToUse: You are adding gestures, sheets, screen transitions or press feedback to an Expo app.
Motion stutters on a real device and you need it on the right thread.
You want haptics that match what the interface is doing.
skills.avoid: For animation on the web, use Web animation.

example.ask: Make the bottom sheet follow my finger and settle with a spring when I let go.
example.outcome: It wires the drag with Gesture Handler, runs the motion on the UI thread with Reanimated and hands off velocity to a spring.

attribution.credit: Written for this catalog, drawing on Emil Kowalski’s design-engineering ideas as inspiration; no source was copied.

skills.name: yeknal-performance
skills.title: App performance
skills.purpose: Measures startup, screen navigation, content loading and scrolling on a throttled production build, finds the real bottleneck, then proves each fix with before and after benchmarks rather than intuition.
skills.description: Make an app faster by measuring startup, navigation, content load, and scroll, fixing the real bottleneck, and proving each win with before and after numbers. Use when an app feels slow to start, to change screens, to fill in, or to scroll.
whenToUse: The app feels slow to start or slow to open a screen.
Content takes too long to appear, especially older or deeper pages.
Scrolling stutters or degrades during a long session.
Every optimization needs a measured before and after.
skills.avoid: It is not failure diagnosis or a motion audit. Use Troubleshoot for a broken feature and Improve animations for motion craft.

example.ask: Make this app faster, benchmark every fix, and tell me what actually worked.
example.outcome: It records a cold production baseline on a throttled device, traces the largest cost, changes one thing at a time, re-measures, and keeps only the wins that clear the noise floor.

skills.name: yeknal-apple-design
skills.title: Apple-style interface design
skills.purpose: Brings Apple’s approach to fluid, physical motion and interface design to the web, from springs and interruptible gestures to materials, depth and typography.
skills.description: Apple-style fluid UI for the web: press response, 1:1 tracking, interruptible springs, velocity handoff, momentum projection, rubber-banding, translucent materials, and optical type. Use for gesture-driven or spring-based interfaces.
whenToUse: You are building drag, swipe or sheet interactions that should feel physical.
You want spring animation and momentum that can be interrupted.
Typography, translucency and depth need the restraint Apple interfaces are known for.

example.ask: Review our swipe-to-dismiss card and make it feel more like iOS.
example.outcome: It checks how the gesture tracks the finger, tunes the spring and velocity hand-off and adds a reduced-motion alternative.

skills.name: yeknal-brandkit
skills.title: Brand kit images
skills.purpose: Generates polished brand-guideline boards, logo systems and identity presentations as images, with deliberate composition and sparse typography.
skills.description: Generate premium brand-kit boards: logo systems, identity decks, and visual-world presentations in a restrained, art-directed style. Use when the user wants a brand kit as an image.
whenToUse: You want visual concepts for a new brand or product identity.
You need a brand-guidelines board to share with a team.
You are exploring logo directions before committing to one.
skills.requirements: Needs an image-generation tool available to your agent.

example.ask: Create a brand board for a calm budgeting app: logo ideas, palette and type.
example.outcome: It plans the identity, then generates a board with logo concepts, colours, type and a couple of mockups.

skills.name: yeknal-break-ui
skills.title: Break UI
skills.purpose: Stress-tests a screen with realistic worst-case data, such as long names, missing fields, huge counts and non-Latin text, and reports every break with its fix.
skills.description: Stress-test a component or screen with realistic worst-case data, put the demo and worst-case states behind a dev-only toggle, and report every break with its fix. Use to break, stress-test, or find UI edge cases.
whenToUse: A screen looks fine with demo data and you want to know where it fails.
You are about to ship a list, table or card that shows user-supplied text.
You want a dev-only toggle between demo and worst-case states.

example.ask: Try the worst case on the team members table.
example.outcome: It fills the table with extreme but realistic data, shows the broken states and fixes overflow, wrapping and empty values.

attribution.credit: Adapted from Emil Kowalski’s skills collection.

skills.name: yeknal-add-changelog
skills.title: Changelog entries
skills.purpose: Adds or updates a Keep a Changelog entry based on the changes and history that can actually be verified, so release notes describe what shipped.
skills.description: Add or update a Keep a Changelog entry from verified changes and history when preparing release notes or recording shipped work.
whenToUse: You are preparing a release and need the notes written up.
Work has shipped and the changelog has fallen behind.
You want entries grouped the Keep a Changelog way under Added, Changed and Fixed.

example.ask: Add a changelog entry for everything merged since the last tag.
example.outcome: It reads the history since that tag, checks what each change actually did and writes a dated entry grouped by type.

skills.name: yeknal-code-graph
skills.title: Code graph
skills.purpose: Builds a local, model-free index of a repository and answers with a small ranked slice, so an unfamiliar codebase can be entered in one call instead of many searches.
skills.description: Use when a task starts in an unfamiliar or large repository and you need the right files in one call instead of many searches. Builds a zero-dependency local index of content terms plus imports, routes and tests, then answers with a small ranked slice inside a token budget. It is retrieval, not GraphRAG, and it never replaces grep for exhaustive matches.
whenToUse: You are starting work in a large repository and do not know where a behavior lives.
The question is conceptual and searching for it would need several vocabulary guesses.
You need call sites, importers, or the tests that touch a route.
skills.avoid: It is not exhaustive and it is not GraphRAG. For every mention of a known identifier, use grep; for a small repository, grep is already one call.

example.ask: In this 300-file app, where does an uploaded CV get turned into text before review?
example.outcome: It builds a local index, returns the parser function and its call sites with line numbers in one call, states that recall is partial, and reads the surrounding code before changing anything.

skills.name: yeknal-yeet
skills.title: Commit, push and open a PR
skills.purpose: Stages, commits, pushes and opens a GitHub pull request in one flow using the GitHub CLI.
skills.description: Use only when the user explicitly asks to stage, commit, push, and open a GitHub pull request in one flow using the GitHub CLI (`gh`).
whenToUse: You want the whole commit-to-PR flow done in one go.
Your changes are ready and reviewed locally.
You use the gh CLI.
skills.avoid: It only runs when you explicitly ask for the full flow.
skills.requirements: Needs the GitHub CLI signed in to your account.

example.ask: Yeet this: commit, push and open a PR.
example.outcome: It stages the changes, writes the commit, pushes the branch and opens a pull request with a summary.

skills.name: yeknal-content-seo
skills.title: Content and SEO
skills.purpose: Guides useful content and search visibility together, from keyword patterns and page briefs to metadata, structured data, sitemaps, local search, earned links and AI citations.
skills.description: Evidence-led search visibility: target queries, update-or-create decisions, metadata, structured data, crawlability, sitemaps, canonicalization, local search, earned links, AI answers (AEO/GEO), and measured citations. Use for SEO, AEO or GEO strategy.
whenToUse: You are choosing which queries to target and which pages should exist.
You are planning or rewriting pages and want them to be found.
Metadata, canonical tags, crawlability or structured data need an audit.
A local business is invisible in the map pack, or links and coverage need a plan.
Traffic moved and you need to separate a ranking loss from a click-through loss.
You want a site to be readable by search engines and AI search alike.

example.ask: Choose the queries worth targeting and tell me whether to update an existing page or create a new one.
example.outcome: It reads the live results, checks existing query and page data, and returns a decision, a brief and the evidence behind it.

skills.name: yeknal-deploy
skills.title: Deploy
skills.purpose: Detects the hosting provider from repository configuration and follows that provider's deploy procedure, so an unnamed "deploy this" request has one entry point instead of four competing ones.
skills.description: Deploy, host, publish, or push a site live to Cloudflare, Netlify, Render, or Vercel, named by the user or detected from repository config. Use when a deploy is requested; keep the first deploy a preview unless production is explicitly asked for.
whenToUse: The user asks to deploy, host, publish or push a site live.
The provider is unstated and has to be read from wrangler, netlify, render or vercel configuration.
A deploy failed and the provider-specific recovery step is needed.
skills.avoid: It is not a hosting comparison and not an infrastructure provisioner. It detects a provider, runs the documented path, and stops to ask when two configurations match.

example.ask: Deploy this app and give me the live link.
example.outcome: It reads the repository configuration, identifies the provider, follows that provider's preview-first procedure, and reports the deployed URL and any missing credentials.

attribution.credit: Provider procedures are adapted from the four previously separate deploy skills, whose licence files moved with the content into references/licenses.

skills.name: yeknal-design-reference-research
skills.title: Design reference research
skills.purpose: Researches comparable products and collects references into an evidence ledger and brief, so design decisions come from what works rather than what’s fashionable.
skills.description: Research interface references into an evidence ledger and implementation brief. Use before design or redesign when references or benchmark evidence should drive direction.
whenToUse: You are about to design or redesign something and want evidence first.
The team disagrees about direction and needs references to compare.
You want patterns from real products, not gallery trends.

example.ask: Research how five scheduling apps handle rescheduling before we redesign ours.
example.outcome: It studies each flow, records what it saw and what it couldn’t verify, and writes a short brief with recommendations.

skills.name: yeknal-design-system
skills.title: Design system
skills.purpose: Builds, audits, documents or migrates a product's design system: token layers, mapping hardcoded values onto tokens, component specs, drift detection and an ordered adoption plan.
skills.description: Build, audit, document, or migrate a product's design system: token layers, mapping hardcoded values onto tokens, component specs, drift detection, and adoption plans. Use when the request names a design system, tokens, component documentation, or inconsistency across an app.
whenToUse: The app has a look but no rules, or the rules live in three places.
You need to know which hardcoded colors, spacing and radii should become tokens.
A component needs a written spec covering anatomy, tokens and states.
The app has drifted off its system and you want an order of work.
You are starting a design system from nothing on a shipped product.

example.ask: Our buttons and cards use slightly different grays and radii. Map them onto tokens and tell me where to start.
example.outcome: It inventories the near-duplicate values, clusters them, proposes role-based tokens with confidence per cluster, and returns an ordered plan with a ratchet so the drift does not return.

skills.name: yeknal-design-taste-frontend
skills.title: Design taste for the web
skills.purpose: Designs and builds expressive landing pages, portfolios and marketing sites from real product evidence instead of reusable AI layouts.
skills.description: Design and build expressive landing pages, portfolios, and marketing interfaces from product evidence instead of reusable AI recipes, including showcase-level art direction. For an existing product use `yeknal-redesign-existing-projects`.
whenToUse: A new web experience needs distinctive art direction and working code.
You want a landing page that doesn’t look like a template.
The brand has a story the layout should carry.
skills.avoid: For an existing product, use Redesign an existing product instead.

example.ask: Design and build a launch page for our note-taking app that feels like ours.
example.outcome: It pulls the visual direction from the product itself, then builds a responsive page with real copy and states.

skills.name: yeknal-domain-modeling
skills.title: Domain modeling
skills.purpose: Clarifies a project’s domain terms and boundaries and records the decisions in a glossary or architecture decision record.
skills.description: Clarify a project's domain concepts and record resolved terminology in a glossary or durable decisions in an ADR. Use when terms, relationships, or system boundaries are ambiguous.
whenToUse: People use different words for the same thing, or one word for two things.
System boundaries are unclear before a larger change.
You want a GLOSSARY.md or an ADR written down.

example.ask: We keep mixing up accounts, workspaces and organisations. Sort out the terms.
example.outcome: It maps how each term is used in code and conversation, proposes definitions and records them in a glossary.

attribution.credit: Written independently, inspired by the domain-modeling skill in Matt Pocock’s skills collection; no source text was copied.

skills.name: yeknal-finalize
skills.title: Finalize
skills.purpose: Runs the final documentation and quality checks, summarises the diff and handles any Git publishing you asked for.
skills.description: Run final documentation and quality gates, summarize the diff, and perform requested Git publication. Use when preparing completed work for delivery.
whenToUse: The work is done and needs a last check before delivery.
You want a clear summary of what changed.
You are ready to commit and push but want the gates run first.

example.ask: Finalize this branch: run the checks, update the docs and push it.
example.outcome: It runs the repository’s checks, updates documentation that the change affects, summarises the diff and pushes.

skills.name: yeknal-find-animation-opportunities
skills.title: Find animation opportunities
skills.purpose: Looks through a codebase or interface for places that should animate and rejects those that shouldn’t, proposing motion with exact values but changing nothing.
skills.description: Search a UI for moments that should animate and reject the rest, with exact values for each surviving suggestion. Read-only; it proposes motion, it does not implement it. For fixes use `yeknal-improve-animations`.
whenToUse: You wonder what could be animated in an app.
An interface feels static and you want it to feel more alive.
You want proposals before anyone writes animation code.
skills.avoid: To fix existing animation, use Improve animations or Review animations.

example.ask: What in the onboarding flow would benefit from motion?
example.outcome: It lists a few specific opportunities with durations and easing, and explains why other spots should stay still.

attribution.credit: Written for this catalog, drawing on Emil Kowalski’s design-engineering ideas as inspiration; no source was copied.

skills.name: yeknal-gh-fix-ci
skills.title: Fix failing CI
skills.purpose: Inspects failing GitHub Actions checks on a pull request, summarises the logs, drafts a fix plan and only makes changes once you approve.
skills.description: Debug failing GitHub PR checks that run in GitHub Actions: inspect checks and logs with `gh`, summarize the failure, propose a fix, and implement after approval. Use when a PR check fails; external providers are out of scope.
whenToUse: Checks are failing on a pull request.
You want the failure explained before anything changes.
CI runs on GitHub Actions.
skills.avoid: Checks from other providers, such as Buildkite, are reported by link only.
skills.requirements: Needs the GitHub CLI signed in to your account.

example.ask: The tests job is failing on my PR. Find out why.
example.outcome: It pulls the failing job’s logs, explains the cause, proposes a fix and waits for your go-ahead.

skills.name: yeknal-oil-motion
skills.title: Frame-based motion
skills.purpose: Designs and builds scrubbable web animation made from generated or captured frames and driven by scroll, pointer, touch or data, for moments ordinary CSS can’t express.
skills.description: Build continuous interactive web animation from generated or captured frames, driven by scroll, pointer, drag, touch, orientation, audio, data, or state. Use when CSS or component motion cannot express a transformation or a scrub-able timeline.
whenToUse: A product transformation or scene change can’t be done with CSS alone.
You want an animation that follows the scroll or the pointer frame by frame.
Media needs processing into an efficient, scrubbable sequence.
skills.avoid: For ordinary UI transitions, use Web animation.
skills.requirements: Frame processing may need Python 3, Pillow and ffmpeg.

example.ask: Make the product photo rotate as the visitor scrolls through the feature section.
example.outcome: It plans the frames, processes them into an efficient sequence and wires playback to the scroll position.

attribution.credit: Adapted from Lin Zhihuang’s oil-motion skill.

skills.name: yeknal-frontend-developer
skills.title: Frontend developer
skills.purpose: Implements or repairs accessible web interfaces in React, Vue or Angular, covering components, state, styling and browser behaviour.
skills.description: Implement or repair web interfaces in React, Vue, or Angular: component architecture, the existing styling system, navigation, and theme persistence. Use for engineering changes, not visual direction.
whenToUse: You are changing frontend components or their state.
A browser behaviour or styling bug needs fixing.
